catalog_quote: In the primary data, the following stress rules apply: (a) Stress a final superheavy syllable CVCC, CCVVC, and CVVC, if present, e.g., krīm ‘kind’, katábt ‘I wrote’, šrúbt ‘I drank’. (b) If no superheavy syllable is present, stress the rightmost non-final heavy syllable CVV or CVC, e.g., safāra ‘embassy’, zábda ‘cotton’. (c) In all other cases, stress the leftmost light syllable CV, e.g., báqara ‘cow’. It is never possible to stress farther left than the antepenultimate syllable, e.g., madrásat-he ‘her school’. ... Analysis of the primary data collected shows that in CVCVC patterns there is a tendency for the first light syllable CV to carry stress, e.g., ˈgamal ‘camel’, ˈgebel ‘mountain’. The behaviour of words like ˈgamal and ˈgebel shows that -CVC syllables in final position count as light and, therefore, do not attract stress. ... sweep_summary: Only one stress-titled bibliography item exists for oman1239 and it is a mis-filing: Bendjaballah & Ségéral 2017 concerns Mehri (Modern South Arabian), not Omani Arabic; it is paywalled at Brill (HAL has only a notice), and it is silent on the catalog coding; priority none for this language (relevant to mehr1241 instead). No new Omani Arabic stress statement was found; As added value, the catalog's deciding source (Morano 2022, OBP, open access) was retrieved from OAPEN (the OBP site is CAPTCHA-walled),, and the deciding quotation was verified verbatim at ch. 2 §5.0, pp. 76-78: weight-sensitive ternary hierarchy (final superheavy > rightmost non-final heavy > leftmost light within the antepenult window, final CVC extrametrical), confirming catalog_kind 'weight'. updated with file -> citation -> URL lines and md5s.

new_statements.reading: Quantity-sensitive (weight) stress with an Arabic-type ternary hierarchy: final superheavy wins; else rightmost non-final heavy (CVV/CVC); else leftmost light, bounded by the antepenult; final CVC is extrametrical (light), giving trochaic ˈCV.CVC. Morano also notes (p. 78, fn. 19) that other Omani varieties (Dhofari per Davey 2016; Muscat per Glover 1988) tend toward iambic/final stress with vowel lengthening, so the al-ʿAwābī rule is not pan-Omani. This is the catalog's existing deciding source, now on file and verified verbatim with page locators; it is a confirmation, not a new source.
